discovery: Quantum logic with trapped ions: the proposal and experimental realization of entangling quantum gates and controlled many-body entanglement in ion strings

nominees.name: Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Rainer Blatt
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: In 1995 Cirac and Zoller showed how laser-cooled ions in a trap, coupled through their shared motion, could implement a universal entangling gate, turning quantum computation from an abstract idea into a concrete experimental program. Blatt and his Innsbruck team realized this blueprint with exceptional technical mastery: the first Cirac-Zoller gate, deterministic teleportation, multi-ion GHZ and W states, and programmable quantum simulation of many-body dynamics. These tools now underpin trapped-ion quantum computers worldwide and, crucially, quantum-logic spectroscopy and entanglement-enhanced optical clocks that push metrology toward and beyond the standard quantum limit. Cirac and Zoller's theory, tightly coupled to experiment, also launched quantum simulation with cold atoms in optical lattices. This is a decades-long program in which precise control of light and matter opened an entirely new domain of physics: engineered, measurable quantum entanglement.
